svg.text: Structured Generation Language - SRT Runtime - RadixAttention - LMSYS / UC Berkeley
Stream decode tokens to text output
CPU prepares next batch while GPU runs current
HTTP server - scheduler - TP worker procs
Rust router - DP / PD / RL coordination
Continuous batching - dynamic add/remove per iter
Chunked prefill - preemption on memory pressure
radix_cache.py - prefix tree for KV reuse
Chained block hash - ref_count per node
Eviction: LRU / LFU / FIFO / MRU / priority
Pre-allocated GPU KV cache memory pool
Encoder cache for VLM vision tokens
CUDA graphs + custom Triton / FlashInfer kernels
Three pillars: RadixAttention (memory) + zero-overhead scheduler (GPU util) + continuous batching (throughput)
Zero-overhead: event_loop_overlap overlaps CPU batch prep with GPU execution
Step 1: recv_requests() - tokenize - add to waiting_queue
Step 2: Radix prefix match - get_computed_blocks - skip cached tokens
Step 3: get_next_batch_to_run() - admit waiting - rebuild running_batch
Step 4: run_batch() - ModelRunner forward + sample on GPU workers
Step 5: process_batch_result() - detokenize - stream - free finished req slots
Prefill + decode mixed in same batch - finished seq slot immediately filled by waiting req
LPM policy prioritizes requests with longest prefix match for max Radix cache hit
Radix tree vs vLLM PagedAttention blocks - dynamic prefix discovery without manual config
Model Gateway - PD Disaggregation + DP Routing
Up to 6x throughput vs alternatives - preferred rollout engine for slime/Miles RL post-training
/update_weights + flush_cache for online RL weight sync - CUDA IPC zero-copy refit
CUDA / ROCm - multi-node TP/PP/DP/EP - K8s / Docker - OpenTelemetry + Prometheus - PyTorch ecosystem
Init path: launch_server - load model - profile mem - init RadixCache + KV pool - spawn scheduler + TP workers
Step path: recv - prefix match - schedule batch - forward - sample - detokenize - cache insert - repeat
Sources: sgl-project/sglang - docs.sglang.io architecture - RadixAttention paper - LMSYS / UC Berkeley
